            Connect to NASA FIRMS

            To download and display NASA FIRMS data, enter your own FIRMS MAP_KEY. Open Data & layers, expand Import NASA FIRMS data, and paste your key.
            READING THE EXPLORER

            Observed points. Possible links.

            Enter a NASA FIRMS MAP_KEY, choose satellites and a UTC date range, then import Canadian detections. FireLedger processes detections in your browser using the Natural Earth 1:10m Canada boundary. The overview groups nearby detections. Zoom in for individual footprints and candidate links.

            The time slider reveals observations and completed links. In 3D, vertical height represents UTC time. The highlighted horizontal plane is your selected moment. Drag the 3D view to rotate; shift-drag to pan.

            A link score is a heuristic compatibility measure, not a percent probability. Apparent speed is the separation of observation centres divided by elapsed time, not measured fire spread. Multiple links may be alternatives or branches; this viewer does not decide which.

            Disks are equal-area approximations of satellite pixels, not fire perimeters or positional-error circles. Brightness values remain instrument-specific. Orange solid links have the highest outgoing score for their source disk (including ties); blue dashed links are alternatives. Darker colours indicate higher scores. These styles do not confirm an association.

            The viewer supports up to 1 million observations and 2 million links; actual performance depends on your browser and graphics hardware. Reduce the export region or time period if importing fails.

            Terrain shows OpenStreetMap features, hillshading and contours where available. The hosted viewer also offers Streets. Natural Earth fills gaps and works offline. Report an OpenStreetMap issue. Drag to move the 2D map or rotate the 3D view. Shift-drag or right-drag to pan in 3D, and use two fingers to pan and pinch on touchscreens.

            Use the buttons in a link’s details to bring that link into view in 2D or 3D. To find a data square, enter longitude and latitude in decimal degrees. For example, −74.5°, 51.2° locates the square from 75°W to 70°W and 50°N to 55°N.

            Open Measure, choose Area or Distance, then click the map to add points. Double-click to finish. Use Pan to explore with measurements visible.
